title: Vegetable Quesadilla
subtitle: Roasted peppers, courgette, and mushrooms with melted cheese
excerpt: Sautéed peppers, courgette (zucchini), and mushrooms with cumin and smoked paprika, packed into flour tortillas with plenty of cheddar and toasted until golden. A vegetarian quesadilla that doesn't need meat to be satisfying.
sourceNotes: Vegetable quesadillas: a vegetarian variation on the Tex-Mex quesadilla, using roasted or sautéed vegetables in place of meat. Based on classic American and Mexican home-cooking traditions.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Sauté the vegetables up to a day ahead; reheat briefly in a pan before filling.

content.text: Vegetable quesadillas are flour tortillas filled with sautéed peppers, courgette, and mushrooms, seasoned with cumin and smoked paprika, and held together by a layer of melted cheddar. The vegetables need to cook down and lose most of their moisture before filling; a wet filling makes the quesadilla soggy. Let them brown properly in a hot pan.
Cook the vegetables in a single pan over high heat, working in batches if needed so they fry rather than steam. Courgette (zucchini) and mushrooms both hold water; they need heat to drive it off.

Heat {{olive-oil}} of oil in a wide frying pan over high heat. Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes. Add the red pepper and courgette slices. Cook for 4-5 minutes without stirring too often, so the vegetables brown rather than steam.
Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic, the mushrooms, cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook for a further 3-4 minutes until the mushrooms are cooked through and the pan is dry. Season with salt. Set aside.
Wipe the pan and set it over medium heat. Lay one flour tortilla flat. Scatter with cheese. Spread half the vegetable mixture over the cheese. Top with a second tortilla and press down.

Cook for 2 minutes until the base is golden, then flip and cook for 1.5-2 minutes on the other side. Rest on a board for 1 minute, then cut into wedges. Repeat with the remaining tortillas and filling. Serve with soured cream and coriander.

items.cause: Vegetables not cooked enough, still releasing water
items.fix: Cook the vegetables in a hot pan until the pan looks dry and the edges of the courgette and mushrooms have started to brown. Wet filling steams the tortilla from inside.

items.symptom: Cheese doesn't bind the quesadilla together
items.cause: Not enough cheese, or grated too coarsely
items.fix: Use finely grated cheddar. It melts faster and coats the vegetables more evenly than large pieces.

items.cause: Not enough cheese relative to vegetable volume
items.fix: Add a bit more cheese or reduce the vegetable quantity slightly; the cheese is what holds the quesadilla together. A moderate filling quantity is easier to cut cleanly.
Medium heat, not high, for the toasting step. The cheese needs 2-3 minutes to melt through a layer of vegetables.

content.text: Add a tin of drained black beans to the vegetable mixture for a more filling quesadilla. Spinach wilted into the pan at the end adds colour without much bulk.

Vegetable quesadillas follow the same structure as every other version; the vegetables carry the spice and the cheese provides the structure. Courgette and mushrooms work particularly well because they take a spice rub and brown easily. The dish is weeknight cooking in the best sense: fast to assemble, flexible with what's in the fridge, and consistently good.
